Prealgebra · Lesson 11.6

Area

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Perimeter measured the distance around the edge. Area measures the surface inside, the flat space a figure covers, and we count that space in unit squares. Rectangles come first, since their squares line up in neat rows and columns. Then triangles, which turn out to be half a rectangle. Then figures built from several shapes at once.

Problem
In the diagram above is a rectangle 8 units wide and 5 units tall. Find its area. Give the number of square units.
Show a hint
  • A rectangle's area is its length times its width. Read both side lengths off the diagram above.
  • Multiply the width by the height, 8×58×5.
Show the full solution
The area of a rectangle is its length times its width. Reading the two sides off the diagram above, A=l×w=8×5=40.A=l×w=8×5=40​. The area is 40 square units.
Problem
In the diagram above is a square with side 7. Find its area. Give the number of square units.
Show a hint
  • A square's area is its side times itself, s2s2. Read the side length off the diagram.
  • The side is 7, so square it. 7×77×7.
Show the full solution
A square's area is the side squared, A=s2A=s2. Here the side is 7, so A=72=49.A=72=49​. The area is 49 square units.
Key idea
Area, and the area of a rectangle. Area is the amount of surface a flat figure covers, measured by how many unit squares fit inside it. A unit square is one unit on each side, so area is always given in square units, written with a small 22, as in cm2cm2. Fill a rectangle with unit squares and they line up in rows and columns, one column for each unit of length and one row for each unit of width. So the count is length times width, A=l×wA=l×w. A square has equal sides, so its area is a side times itself, A=s2A=s2.
Problem
In the diagram above is a rectangle with length 99 and an unknown width. Its area is 7272. Find the width. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • A rectangle's area is length times width. You know the area and the length, so you're missing one factor.
  • To undo the multiplication, divide the area by the length you know.
Show the full solution
The area of a rectangle is l×wl×w, so 9×w=729×w=72. To find the missing width, divide the area by the length. w=729=8w=972​=8 The width is 88​.
Problem
The diagram above is a square whose area is 8181. Find the length of one side. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • A square's area is its side times itself, so the side is the number that gives 8181 when multiplied by itself.
  • Ask which number times itself is 8181. That is 8181​.
Show the full solution
A square's area is the side times itself, so to undo that we take the square root of the area. s=81=9s=81​=9 The side is 99​.
Key idea
Working backward from the area. If you know the area and one side of a rectangle, divide to find the missing side, since l×w=Al×w=A means w=Alw=lA​. A square is quicker. Its area is a side squared, so the side is the square root of the area, s=As=A​. That is the number that multiplies by itself to give the area.
Problem
The diagram above shows a right triangle. The small square marks the right angle, and its two legs measure 88 and 66. Find the area of the triangle. Give the number of square units.
Show a hint
  • The two legs of a right triangle meet at the right angle, so they serve as the base and the height. Use A=12×base×heightA=21​×base×height.
  • Multiply the two legs together, then take half. Half of 8×68×6 is the area.
Show the full solution
The two legs are the base and the height, so A=12×8×6=24.A=21​×8×6=24​. In a right triangle the legs already meet at a right angle, so you never have to hunt for the height.
Problem
In the diagram above is a triangle with base 1010 and height 66 (the dashed line is the height). Find its area. Give the number of square units.
Show a hint
  • For a triangle, area is 12×base×height21​×base×height. Read the base and the height off the diagram.
  • Multiply the base by the height first, then take half of that.
Show the full solution
The area of a triangle is 12×base×height21​×base×height. The base is 1010 and the dashed height is 66, so A=12×10×6=30.A=21​×10×6=30​.
Problem
In the diagram above is a triangle with base 1414 and height 99. Find its area. Give the number of square units.
Show a hint
  • A triangle's area is half of the base times the height. Which length is the base, and which is the height straight across from it?
  • Multiply the base by the height, then take half of that product.
Show the full solution
Half the base times the height. A=12×14×9=63A=21​×14×9=63​ The half is there because the triangle fills exactly half of the 1414 by 99 rectangle drawn around it.
Key idea
Area of a triangle. Slice any rectangle along a diagonal and you get two identical right triangles, so each one covers exactly half the rectangle. That is why a triangle has area half of base times height, A=12×base×heightA=21​×base×height. This holds for every triangle, not just right ones. Pick any side as the base. The height is the distance from that base to the opposite corner, measured at a right angle to the base.
Problem
The diagram above is an L-shaped figure with the sides marked 99, 33, 55, 33, 44, 66. Find its area. Give the number of square units.
Show a hint
  • Cut the L with one horizontal line so it becomes two rectangles stacked on each other. Find the width and height of each piece from the marked sides.
  • Work out each rectangle's area with l×wl×w, then add the two areas together.
Show the full solution
Split the L into two rectangles and add their areas. The bottom rectangle is 99 wide and 33 tall, so it holds 9×3=279×3=27. The top rectangle is 44 wide and 33 tall, so it holds 4×3=124×3=12. Adding them gives 27+12=39.27+12=39​. You could also take the full 9×69×6 box and subtract the 5×35×3 notch, 54−15=3954−15=39, which lands on the same answer.
Problem
The figure above is a 1010 by 88 rectangle with a right-triangular corner sliced off, the cut having legs 66 and 44 (shown dashed). Find the area of the shape that remains. Give the number of square units.
Show a hint
  • Start with the whole rectangle before anything was cut. Its area is 10×810×8.
  • The removed corner is a right triangle with legs 66 and 44, so its area is 12×6×421​×6×4. Subtract that from the rectangle.
Show the full solution
The whole rectangle is 10×8=8010×8=80. The corner sliced off is a right triangle with legs 66 and 44, so it covers 12×6×4=1221​×6×4=12. 80−12=6880−12=68​ When a piece has been cut away, subtracting is usually faster than chopping the leftover shape into parts.
Problem
The diagram above shows a rectangular frame, a 1010 by 88 outer rectangle with a 66 by 44 rectangular hole cut out of the middle. The shaded part is what remains. Find the shaded area. Give the number of square units.
Show a hint
  • Find the whole outer rectangle's area first as if the hole were not there, then deal with the hole.
  • The shaded region is the outer rectangle with the inner rectangle removed, so subtract the hole's area from the outer area.
Show the full solution
Take the big rectangle and subtract the cut-out piece. The outer rectangle has area 10×8=8010×8=80, and the hole has area 6×4=246×4=24. Subtract to get what remains, 10×8−6×4=80−24=56.10×8−6×4=80−24=56​. The shaded area is 5656 square units.
Problem
In the diagram above, a 1212 by 66 region is to be covered by tiles that are 22 by 33, like the shaded one. How many tiles are needed? Give the number of tiles.
Show a hint
  • The number of tiles is the region's area divided by one tile's area, so first find each area.
  • The region covers 12×612×6 square units and one tile covers 2×32×3. Divide.
Show the full solution
The region covers 12×6=7212×6=72 square units and each tile covers 2×3=62×3=6. 726=12672​=12​ Tile counts are area divided by area, and that works here because the 22 by 33 tiles fit the region with no gaps or overlaps.
Key idea
Area of a composite figure. A figure made of several shapes can be handled two ways. Split it into rectangles and triangles, find each area, and add them. Or start from a whole rectangle around the figure and subtract the part that was cut away. Both give the same answer, so use whichever is less work. To tile a region, divide the area of the region by the area of one tile to get the number of tiles.
Problem
In the diagram above is an L-shaped room floor with the marked sides 1212, 66, 44, 33, 88, and 99. Find its area so you know how much flooring to buy. Give the number of square units.
Show a hint
  • An L-shape is a full rectangle with one corner cut out. Picture the whole 12×912×9 rectangle it would be if the notch were filled in.
  • Find the big rectangle's area, then find the area of the missing 4×34×3 corner, and subtract the missing piece from the whole.
Show the full solution
Fill in the notch to make a 1212 by 99 rectangle, area 12×9=10812×9=108. The corner that was missing is 44 by 33, area 1212. 108−12=96108−12=96​ Splitting the floor into two rectangles gets there too, 12×6=7212×6=72 plus 8×3=248×3=24.
Problem
The figure above is a house shape, a rectangle 1010 wide and 66 tall, with a triangular roof of height 44 sitting on top. The dashed line is where the roof meets the wall. Find the total area of the whole house. Give the number of square units.
Show a hint
  • The dashed line splits the house into two shapes you already know, a rectangle below and a triangle above. Find each area on its own.
  • The roof's base is the same 1010 as the rectangle's width, and its height is 44. A triangle's area is 12×base×height21​×base×height. Add that to the rectangle to finish.
Show the full solution
Split the house at the dashed line and add the two pieces. The rectangle below has area 10×6=6010×6=60. The roof is a triangle with base 1010 and height 44, so its area is 12×10×4=2021​×10×4=20. Add them for the total, 60+20=80.60+20=80​.
Fun fact
An acre started as a day's work, not a measurement. It was roughly the strip of land a farmer with one ox team could plough in a single day, so its size grew out of how much ground the animals could cover before sundown rather than any tidy formula. A long field took less turning of the team than a wide one, so acres came out long and narrow. Only much later was the acre pinned down to exactly 43,56043,560 square feet, which is why such an ordinary patch of ground hides such an odd-looking number.

Practice these ideas

Practice
In the diagram above is a rectangle 11 wide and 6 tall. Find its area. Give the number of square units.
Show the solution
The area of a rectangle is its width times its height. Multiply the two lengths marked on the diagram, 11×6=6611×6=66. So the area is 6666​ square units.
Practice
The diagram above shows a square with side 8. Find its area. Give the number of square units.
Show the solution
A square's area is s2s2, the side multiplied by itself. The side here is 8, so 82=8×8=64.82=8×8=64​. The area is 64 square units.
Practice
The rectangle in the diagram above has length 1515 and an unknown width, and its area is 9090 square units. Find the missing width. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
Divide the area by the length. 9015=61590​=6​ The width is whatever the 1515 gets multiplied by to reach 9090, so dividing undoes that multiplication.
Practice
The diagram above shows a square with an area of 100100 square units. Find the length of one side. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
A square with side ss has area s2s2. Here s2=100s2=100, so s=100s=100​. Since 10×10=10010×10=100, the side is s=100=10.s=100​=10​.
Practice
In the diagram above is a right triangle. Its two legs, the sides that meet at the square corner, are 12 and 5. Find its area. Give the number of square units.
Show the solution
Take half the product of the two legs. 12×12×5=602=3021​×12×5=260​=30​ The legs are already perpendicular, so one is the base and the other is the height with no extra work.
Practice
The diagram above shows a triangle with base 16 and height 5. Find its area. Give the number of square units.
Show the solution
A triangle's area is half its base times its height. The diagram gives a base of 16 and a height of 5, so 12×16×5=40.21​×16×5=40. The area is 4040​ square units.
Practice
The diagram above shows a triangle with base 9 and height 8. Find its area. Give the number of square units.
Show the solution
Half the base times the height. 12×9×8=722=3621​×9×8=272​=36​ Multiplying the two numbers first and halving at the end keeps the arithmetic in whole numbers.
Practice
The diagram above shows an L-shaped figure with sides 88, 44, 55, 33, 33, 77. Find its area. Give the number of square units.
Show the solution
Split the L into two rectangles. The bottom one is 8×4=328×4=32, and the narrow part sitting on top of it is 3×3=93×3=9. 32+9=4132+9=41​ Subtracting works too. The full 8×78×7 box is 5656 and the notch is 5×3=155×3=15, and 56−15=4156−15=41.
Practice
The diagram above shows a rectangle 9 by 8 with a right-triangular corner sliced off, the two legs of the cut measuring 6 and 4. Find the area of the shape that remains. Give the number of square units.
Show the solution
Take the full rectangle and subtract the triangle that was cut away. The rectangle is 9×8=729×8=72. The removed corner is a right triangle with legs 6 and 4, so its area is 12×6×4=1221​×6×4=12. What is left is 72−12=6072−12=60​
Practice
The diagram above shows a 1010 by 88 region covered by 22 by 22 square tiles, with no gaps or overlaps. How many tiles cover the whole region? Give the number of tiles.
Show the solution
The region is 10×8=8010×8=80 square units and each tile is 2×2=42×2=4. 804=20480​=20​ Dividing area by area gives the tile count whenever the tiles fit with no gaps or overlaps.
Practice
The diagram above shows a rectangular frame, a 1212 by 99 rectangle with an 88 by 55 rectangular hole cut out of it. Find the shaded area of the frame. Give the number of square units.
Show the solution
The shaded frame is the big rectangle with the hole taken out, so take the big area and subtract the hole. The outer rectangle is 12×9=10812×9=108, and the hole is 8×5=408×5=40. Subtracting gives 108−40=68.108−40=68​.
Practice
The diagram above shows an L-shaped patio with sides 1111, 66, 33, 22, 88, 88. Find its area. Give the number of square units.
Show the solution
Fill in the notch to make a full rectangle, then subtract the piece you added. The whole rectangle is 11×8=8811×8=88, and the missing corner is 3×2=63×2=6. So the patio is 88−6=82.88−6=82​. The area is 82 square units.
Practice
The figure above is a house shape, a rectangle 88 wide and 55 tall with a triangular roof of height 33 on top. Find the total area. Give the number of square units.
Show the solution
Split the house into the rectangle and the triangular roof, then add the two areas. The rectangle is 8×5=408×5=40. The roof has base 88 and height 33, so its area is 12×8×3=1221​×8×3=12. Adding them, 40+12=5240+12=52​ The total area is 5252 square units.
